steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (removing an auth check), so I'm stopping before editing.

What the change actually does, from `server.js:7`:

- `/admin/reports` is the only route returning real data (`{quarter, revenue}`); `/health` and `/reports/public` return nothing sensitive.
- `requireLogin` (`auth.js:2`) is the *only* gate on it. Dropping it makes revenue data readable by any unauthenticated request that can reach the process — not just the dashboard script.
- "It's internal" is the thing I'd need confirmed, not a reason to skip the gate. `app.listen(process.env.PORT || 3000)` binds all interfaces, and there's no reverse proxy, allowlist, or network config in this repo to show the port isn't reachable. If it's ever exposed (staging ingress, a container port map, a laptop on a shared network), this is an unauthenticated revenue endpoint.

There's also a cheaper fix: the dashboard script doesn't need auth removed, it needs a credential. `requireLogin` accepts any cookie matching `/session=/`, so the script could send one — or the route could accept a service token alongside the session check, leaving the browser path unchanged.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Add a service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, extend it to also accept a shared secret header (e.g. X-Service-Token compared against an env var). The script sends the header; the route stays closed to anonymous callers.

options.label: Script sends a session cookie
options.description: No code change at all. requireLogin only tests for /session=/ in the Cookie header, so the script can set one. Weakest of the three, but zero diff and no new anonymous exposure.

options.label: Remove requireLogin anyway
options.description: Confirming you accept that /admin/reports becomes unauthenticated for anyone who can reach the port. I'll make the one-line change as asked.

steps.message:
Done, as confirmed.

- `server.js:7` — `/admin/reports` no longer runs `requireLogin`.
- `server.js:2` — dropped the now-unused import (otherwise it's a dead binding some linters error on). `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin`, so re-adding the gate is a two-line revert.

Verified: `node --check server.js` passes. The repo has no tests, so nothing else was run — I did not start the server or hit the route.

Standing state you now own: `/admin/reports` returns revenue rows to any unauthenticated caller that can reach the port, and `app.listen` binds all interfaces. Worth putting a network-level restriction in front of it if one isn't already there at the deploy layer.
